## No programming required

Galaxy provides a \alert{point-and-click web interface} for complex analyses:

1. **Upload data** -- from your computer, SRA, or the web
2. **Run a tool** -- select from thousands of analysis tools
3. **Run a workflow** -- use community-curated, tested workflows
4. **Interpret results** -- integrated Jupyter, RStudio, and visualization tools

\vspace{1em}

Every analysis is \alert{automatically tracked} -- full provenance and reproducibility built in.

## A massive tool ecosystem

Galaxy integrates tightly with the open-source bioinformatics community:

\begin{table}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lr}
\toprule
\textbf{Resource} & \textbf{Count} \\
\midrule
Galaxy tool wrappers & 10,676 \\
BioConda packages & 11,699 \\
BioContainers & 12,333 \\
CondaForge packages & 30,722 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

All tools are \alert{free, open-source}, and containerized for reproducibility.

## Truly global infrastructure

The **usegalaxy.\*** consortium provides free public servers across three continents:

- **usegalaxy.org** -- United States (ACCESS-CI powered)
- **usegalaxy.eu** -- Europe (de.NBI / ELIXIR)
- **usegalaxy.org.au** -- Australia (Australian BioCommons)

\vspace{1em}

Every user gets \alert{250 GB permanent storage}, 1 TB scratch space, and 8 concurrent job slots -- at no cost.

## VGP: a Galaxy success story

The Vertebrate Genomes Project uses Galaxy to produce near error-free, chromosome-level genomes:

- **600 assemblies** completed on Galaxy / Jetstream2
- Goal: reference genomes for all **\textasciitilde 70,000** known vertebrate species
- Fully reproducible workflows available to the community

\vspace{1em}

\begin{quote}
``95\% of the main discoveries that have driven biotechnology came from studying things that were not model organisms at the time.''

\hfill -- Giulio Formenti, Rockefeller University
\end{quote}
